title: The ethics of AI
examples: If an AI car causes an accident, who is at fault?
How can we make sure AI is fair to everyone?
Will AI take away all our jobs in the future?

explain.say: Today we will talk about the ethics of artificial intelligence.

draw.text: AI Ethics: Bias, Responsibility, Privacy, Jobs

explain.say: First we look at bias in artificial intelligence systems.
Bias happens when the data used is not fair.
Next we consider the issue of responsibility when AI fails.
We must also think about personal privacy with AI systems.
Finally, AI raises questions about future jobs and work.

faq.q: If an AI makes a mistake, who is legally responsible?
faq.a: Currently, responsibility is debated among the programmer, the owner, and the user. Some argue that accountability must be assigned to a human party.
asks: Who is to blame when AI fails?
Can AI be held legally responsible?

faq.q: How can we stop AI from showing bias?
faq.a: We must ensure that the data used to train AI models is diverse and representative of all groups of people. This requires careful auditing of datasets.
asks: What is the best way to remove bias?
How do we make AI fair?

faq.q: What does 'data privacy' mean in the context of AI?
faq.a: It means controlling who can collect your personal information and how that information is used by AI systems. You should know what data is being taken.
asks: Are my personal details safe from AI?
What is data ownership with AI?

faq.q: Will AI take away all the jobs people have?
faq.a: It is more likely that AI will change jobs rather than eliminate all of them. New jobs requiring human skills will also be created.
asks: Are robots taking all the jobs?

faq.q: Is bias only a problem in facial recognition AI?
faq.a: No, bias can appear in many areas, such as loan applications or medical diagnoses, if the underlying data is skewed.
asks: Can bias happen outside of images?
Where else can AI be biased?

facts: AI systems learn patterns from vast amounts of data provided by humans.
Bias in AI often reflects existing human biases present in the training data.
Data privacy concerns focus on the collection and use of personal information.
Automation through AI is expected to change job roles, not necessarily eliminate all work.

quiz.say: If an AI medical diagnostic tool consistently misses symptoms in one demographic group, this is an example of:
quiz.why: The failure to perform equally across groups shows the data was not representative.

wrong.1: Privacy relates to data collection, not performance gaps.
wrong.2: Responsibility is about blame, not the pattern of error.
wrong.3: This term relates to employment, not diagnostic accuracy.

quiz.say: When an AI system uses your voice patterns to unlock your phone, which ethical principle is most concerned?
quiz.why: Using unique personal identifiers like voice patterns is a major privacy concern.

wrong.1: Bias would mean it only works for certain voices, but the core issue is data use.
wrong.2: Responsibility is about who is accountable after a problem occurs.
wrong.3: This concept is unrelated to biometric data security.

quiz.say: A self-driving car causes an accident because its sensors were trained mostly in sunny weather, failing in the rain. This highlights issues of:
quiz.why: The system performs poorly under conditions different from its training data.

wrong.1: The accident itself does not primarily concern personal data leaks.
wrong.2: This scenario is about immediate safety failure, not employment.
wrong.3: While accountability is involved, the root cause shown is the biased training.
